claims.text: For \(r,q\ge1\), with \(A=\Lambda/I_{r,q}\) the \(q^r\)-box quotient, \[ A\cong\mathbb Z[h_1,\ldots,h_q]/(e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}), \] where \(E(-t)H(t)=1\). Indeed, \[ I_{r,q}=(h_{q+1},h_{q+2},\ldots,e_{r+1},\ldots,e_{r+q}). \]
For the \(i=j=1\) case, \(J_v=A_+\), and, with \(m=\min(r,q)\), \[ A_+/A_+^2\cong\bigoplus_{k=1}^{m}\mathbb Z\,\overline h_k\cong\mathbb Z^m. \]
In \(A_+/A_+^2\), \[ \overline e_k=(-1)^{k-1}\overline h_k\qquad(1\le k\le m). \] Hence both \(\{h_1,\ldots,h_m\}\) and \(\{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}\) map to integral bases.

The two specialized families are \[ \{h_1,\ldots,h_m\},\qquad \{e_1,\ldots,e_m\}; \] each minimally generates \(J_v=A_+\). Thus the \(i=j=1\) family, equivalently \(v_{r,r,r,r+q}\) for \(r,q\ge1\), is settled.
The supplied project documentation records the corresponding free-indecomposables assertion as only suspected in the general rectangular case. [source-6@L56-L70|claim=ordinary-document]
